sentences.zh: 而且因为我是个好纳粹和建制派的中流砥柱，我有过这家伙，我会带他在公共场合吃饭，请他吃午餐。

sentences.en: And there was absolutely no scandal, no impropriety, nothing like this.
sentences.zh: 绝对没有任何丑闻，没有任何不正当行为，没有诸如此类的事。

sentences.en: People like Wilhelm Keitel, who was at his side throughout the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 像威廉·凯特尔这样在整个二战期间一直陪伴在他身边的.

sentences.zh: 瓦尔特·冯·布劳希奇。

sentences.zh: 他们是他的傀儡。

sentences.zh: 所以现在希特勒，我的意思是，他已经掌握了国家的所有大权，但现在他也是军队的领袖了。

sentences.en: And there's no one to oppose him at all.

sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.zh: 汤姆，我们花这么长时间讨论这个原因在于，这是接下来发生的事情的关键先决条件。

sentences.en: There is basically nobody to stand in his way.
sentences.zh: 基本上没有人能阻挡他的路。

sentences.en: So let's get into the issue of Austria.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们进入奥地利的问题。

sentences.en: So we're into 1938 and Hitler is eyeing up Austria, his southern neighbor.
sentences.zh: 所以我们进入了1938年，希特勒正盯着奥地利，他的南部邻居。

sentences.en: Now, of course, Hitler was born in Austria, brought up in Austria.
sentences.zh: 现在，当然，希特勒出生在奥地利，在奥地利长大。

sentences.en: Hitler is, to all intents and purposes, Austrian.
sentences.zh: 无论从哪个角度来看，希特勒都是奥地利人。

sentences.en: And before the First World War, when he'd been growing up, he had been a passionate pan-German.
sentences.zh: 在第一次世界大战之前，当他成长的时候，他曾是一个充满激情的泛德意志主义者。

sentences.en: So he'd been one of these people who thought, I hate the Habsburgs.
sentences.zh: 所以他是那种认为我恨哈布斯堡王朝的人之一。

sentences.en: I hate the Czechs, the Slovenes, all these other people.
sentences.zh: 我恨捷克人、斯洛文尼亚人以及所有这些其他人。

sentences.en: I don't like the multiculturalism of Vienna that we, looking at it from 2023, think is so brilliant.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢维也纳的多元文化主义，而我们从2023年的角度来看觉得它是如此辉煌。

sentences.en: And I hate all that.
sentences.zh: 我恨所有这一切。

sentences.en: I wish we could turn our back on all these kind of Slavs and Hungarians and Jews who I don't like.
sentences.zh: 我希望我们能背弃所有这些我不喜欢的斯拉夫人和匈牙利人以及犹太人。

sentences.en: This is Adolf Hitler speaking, obviously.
sentences.zh: 显然后面说这话的是阿道夫·希特勒。

sentences.en: And I wish German Austria, the kind of Austrian heartland, could be united with Germany.
sentences.zh: 我希望德意志奥地利，也就是奥地利的核心地带，能够与德国统一。

sentences.en: And in those days, he would have thought under the Hohenzollerns, not under the Habsburgs.
sentences.zh: 在那个年代，他会认为是根据霍亨索伦王朝，而不是根据哈布斯堡王朝。

sentences.en: And that dream of a kind of pan-German unity has never left him at all.
sentences.zh: 那种泛德意志统一的梦想从未离开过他。

sentences.en: And obviously, there's a lot of other people in Austria who think that too.
sentences.zh: 显然，奥地利还有很多其他人也这样认为。

sentences.en: So when the Habsburg Empire fell apart in 1918, all the other bits fell away.
sentences.zh: 所以当哈布斯堡帝国在1918年崩溃时，所有其他部分都脱离了。

sentences.en: There'd been 54 million people in the Habsburg Empire.
sentences.zh: 哈布斯堡帝国曾有5400万人口。

sentences.en: And now there's only 7 million of them left.
sentences.zh: 而现在只剩下700万人了。

sentences.en: And they're German speakers.
sentences.zh: 而且他们是说德语的人。

sentences.en: And they think, well, we don't want to live in a country called Austria.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，好吧，我们不想生活在一个叫奥地利的国家。

sentences.en: We actually want to live in Germany.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上想生活在德国。

sentences.en: And obviously, the big thing at the end of the First World War is about national self-determination.
sentences.zh: 显然，第一次世界大战结束时的重大议题是关于民族自决的。

sentences.en: And it is a tiny bit unjust that the Allies said, absolutely everybody else, the Czechs, the Serbs, whatever, they can all have national self-determination, but you can't.
sentences.zh: 盟国说，绝对所有人，捷克人、塞尔维亚人，无论什么人，都可以拥有民族自决权，但唯独你们不能，这其实有一点点不公平。

sentences.en: So you cannot join Germany.
sentences.zh: 所以你们不能加入德国。

sentences.en: For very obvious reasons.
sentences.zh: 原因显而易见。

sentences.en: Yeah, because they don't want Germany to become bigger.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为他们不想让德国变得更大。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Which is precisely why Hitler wants to absorb Austria, presumably.
sentences.zh: 这正是希特勒想要吞并奥地利的原因，想必如此。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: The Austrians actually originally wanted to call their country German-Austria.
sentences.zh: 奥地利人最初实际上想把他们的国家叫做德意志奥地利。

sentences.en: And the Allies, in the Treaty of Saint-Germain, they actually banned them from choosing the name for their own country.
sentences.zh: 而盟国在《圣日耳曼条约》中，实际上禁止他们为自己的国家选择这个名字。

sentences.en: They had to call it Austria rather than German-Austria.
sentences.zh: 他们不得不把它叫做奥地利，而不是德意志奥地利。

sentences.en: It's just this sort of appendix.
sentences.zh: 它就像是这样一个附庸。

sentences.en: I mean, we now think of Austria as part of the European map.

sentences.en: But at the time, people just thought of it as this weird leftover.

sentences.zh: 唱歌的修女。

sentences.zh: 他对此坚信不疑。

sentences.en: One blood demands one Reich.
sentences.zh: 同一血脉要求同一个帝国。

sentences.en: Now, the Austrians themselves, as time goes on, they become a little bit divided about this.
sentences.zh: 现在，随着时间的推移，奥地利人自己对此也产生了一些分歧。

sentences.en: So particularly Catholics in Austria are a bit anxious about allying with Nazi Germany.
sentences.zh: 因此，特别是奥地利的天主教徒对与纳粹德国结盟感到有些担忧。

sentences.en: Well, yeah, for understandable reasons.
sentences.zh: 好吧，是的，出于可以理解的原因。

sentences.zh: 天主教会和纳粹政权之间一直存在着很多紧张关系。

sentences.en: They don't want to be necessarily dragged into Hitler's orbit.
sentences.zh: 他们不希望一定被拉入希特勒的势力范围。

sentences.zh: 但到1933年左右，奥地利基本上滑向了一个由恩格尔bert·多尔弗斯统治的法团主义、天主教、威权独裁政权，他是一个来自奥地利乡村的充满热情的炽热天主教徒。

sentences.en: Now, this has slightly been rigged.
sentences.zh: 现在，这稍微有点被操纵的成分。

sentences.en: A lot of workplaces and factories have closed and employees have been told they will be paid anyway, but they have to go to join the crowd.
sentences.zh: 许多工作场所和工厂已经关闭，员工被告知无论如何都会发工资，但他们必须去加入人群。

sentences.en: But all of that said, even Ian Kershaw, who really goes into all this, says, the enthusiasm is not contrived.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，甚至连深入研究过这一切的伊恩·克肖也表示，这种热情并非做作。

sentences.en: The enthusiasm is genuine.
sentences.zh: 这种热情是真诚的。

sentences.en: Hitler is on the balcony, once again, of the Hotel Imperial, and then he gives a speech in the
sentences.zh: 希特勒再次站在帝国酒店的阳台上，然后他在

sentences.en: Heldenplatz.
sentences.zh: 英雄广场发表了演讲。

sentences.en: There are vast, vast crowds of youngsters who are screaming and cheering and sobbing.
sentences.zh: 有成群结队、浩浩荡荡的年轻人尖叫、欢呼并啜泣。

sentences.en: Every Catholic church in the city is flying the swastika on the orders of their local cardinal, Cardinal Initzer, who's the Archbishop of Vienna.
sentences.zh: 在维也纳大主教、当地枢机主教因尼策的命令下，城里的每一座天主教教堂都悬挂着纳粹旗帜。

sentences.en: They can't sleep, the Nazis, in the hotel.
sentences.zh: 纳粹分子在酒店里根本睡不着觉。

sentences.en: It's very Beatlemania.
sentences.zh: 这非常像披头士狂热。

sentences.en: They can't sleep because people are outside cheering them and screaming and saying, we want to see the Führer.
sentences.zh: 他们睡不着觉，因为外面的人在为他们欢呼、尖叫，并喊着：我们想见元首。

sentences.en: Sending the chambermaids in to steal the sheets and...
sentences.zh: 派女服务员进去偷床单，然后……

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: ...slip them up and sell them as souvenirs and all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: ……把它们撕碎当作纪念品出售以及诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: It's an extraordinary, extraordinary scene.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非同寻常、叹为观止的场景。

sentences.en: And for Hitler, it's...
sentences.zh: 对希特勒来说，这……

sentences.en: Apotheosis, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我想，这就是全盛期。

sentences.en: Absolute apotheosis.
sentences.zh: 绝对的巅峰状态。

sentences.en: Totally invigorating.
sentences.zh: 极大地振奋了精神。

sentences.en: So it won't be doing anything to stop his messiah complex?
sentences.zh: 所以这不会对阻止他的救世主情结起到任何作用咯？

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 一点也不会。

sentences.en: He eventually goes back to Berlin.
sentences.zh: 他最终回到了柏林。

sentences.en: They have a big plebiscite, both in Germany and in Austria.
sentences.zh: 他们在德国和奥地利都举行了盛大的全民公投。

sentences.en: Both results, 99% plus.
sentences.zh: 两个结果都是百分之九十九以上。

sentences.en: Vote yes.
sentences.zh: 投票赞成。

sentences.en: You know, there's obviously the usual intimidation and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这其中显然有通常的恐吓等等。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But, as Kershaw says, for the mass of the German people, Hitler once more seemed a statesman of extraordinary, virtuoso talents.
sentences.zh: 但是，正如克肖所说，对于广大德国人民来说，希特勒再次展现出了一位拥有非凡大师级才能的政治家的风范。

sentences.en: You know, he has pulled off an extraordinary coup.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他完成了一次非凡的政变。

sentences.en: And for the Austrians.
sentences.zh: 而对于奥地利人来说。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: They've kind of voted with great enthusiasm for this.
sentences.zh: 他们以极大的热情对这一切投了赞成票。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Beatlemania scenes, all this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 披头士狂热的场景，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: But, as we said earlier, the Nazi high command are basically set on plundering Austria, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 但是，正如我们刚才所说，纳粹高层基本上是打定主意要掠夺奥地利，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So how long does it take the Austrians to realise what they've actually signed up to?
sentences.zh: 那么，奥地利人花了多长时间才意识到他们实际上签下了什么？

sentences.en: Weeks, months, maybe.
sentences.zh: 几周，几个月，也许吧。

sentences.en: They're not equal partners at all.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不是平等的伙伴。

sentences.en: They're merely the Eastern March, Ostmark is what they're called.
sentences.zh: 他们仅仅被称为东部边疆区，德语里叫Ostmark。

sentences.en: And eventually, in 1942, the Ostmark itself is divided into two Reich regions, the Alps and the Danube.
sentences.zh: 最终，在1942年，东部边疆区本身被划分为两个帝国大区，即阿尔卑斯和多瑙河大区。

sentences.en: So Austria vanishes completely from the map.
sentences.zh: 因此，奥地利从地图上彻底消失了。

sentences.en: Austria completely vanishes from the map.
sentences.zh: 奥地利从地图上彻底消失了。

sentences.en: The local Austrian Nazis, for whom this had been a moment, you know, long dreamed of, they end up being supplanted by people sent from Berlin.
sentences.zh: 当地的奥地利纳粹分子——对他们来说，这曾是一个梦寐以求的时刻——最终被从柏林派来的人取代了。

sentences.en: So a measure of poetic justice there, then?
sentences.zh: 那么，这算是一种因果报应的诗意正义吗？

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: All the Austrian institutions, the railways, the banks, the postal service, everything else, the army, all these things.
sentences.zh: 所有奥地利的机构，铁路、银行、邮政服务、其他一切、军队，所有这些东西。

sentences.en: They lose their meaning.
sentences.zh: 它们都失去了意义。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And they end up being bossed around and treated like kind of country bumpkins.
sentences.zh: 他们最后被颐指气使，被当成乡巴佬对待。

sentences.en: And the iron ore?
sentences.zh: 还有铁矿石呢？

sentences.en: And of course, the iron ore, which Goering wanted, that's taken to Germany.
sentences.zh: 当然，戈林想要的铁矿石被运到了德国。

sentences.en: He gets his fat hands on it.
sentences.zh: 他把贪婪的双手伸向了它。

sentences.en: He gets his fat hands on the gold in Vienna, the Viennese banks, gold, their foreign currency reserves, even art is taken.
sentences.zh: 他将贪婪的双手伸向了维也纳的黄金、维也纳银行的黄金、他们的外汇储备，甚至连艺术品都被抢走了。

sentences.en: So the classic example of this, we alluded to this in the Nuremberg Morales episodes, the crown jewels of the Holy Roman Empire are taken from Vienna to Nuremberg.
sentences.zh: 所以这方面的经典例子——我们在纽伦堡审判的剧集中也提到过——神圣罗马帝国的皇冠明珠被从维也纳运到了纽伦堡。

sentences.en: So they'd been moved from Nuremberg, hadn't they, to Vienna?
sentences.zh: 所以它们以前是从纽伦堡搬到维也纳去的，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And now they get them back.
sentences.zh: 而现在他们把它们拿回去了。

sentences.en: So they won't be bothering with replicas anymore.
sentences.zh: 所以他们以后不用再用复制品凑合了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: All this kind of, you know, the Nazis moving in, removing industrial capacity, removing the gold reserves from the bank, plundering the art.
sentences.zh: 所有这些，你知道的，纳粹进驻，搬走工业产能，移走银行的黄金储备，掠夺艺术品。

sentences.en: But this is the prototype for what will happen in the Nazi occupation of Europe during the Second World War, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但这正是第二次世界大战期间纳粹占领欧洲时将要发生的事情的原型，对吧？

sentences.en: So to that extent, the way that Austria, after the war, presents itself as the first victim of the Nazi wars of conquest, I mean, it's not inaccurate.
sentences.zh: 从这个角度来看，奥地利在战后把自己包装成纳粹征服战争的第一个受害者，我的意思是，这并非不准确。

sentences.en: To that degree, it's not inaccurate.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这并非不准确。

sentences.en: So obviously, the cheering crowds don't sit easily.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，欢呼的人群与此并不太搭。

sentences.en: Yes, that's an embarrassment.
sentences.zh: 是的，这很尴尬。

sentences.en: Yeah, and then massive enthusiasm.
sentences.zh: 对，还有那巨大的热情。

sentences.en: But it's like being kind of swept off your feet by a very seductive boyfriend.
sentences.zh: 但这就像是被一个极具魅力的男朋友迷得神魂颠倒一样。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then finding that he's nicking all your money and beating you up.
sentences.zh: 然后发现他把你所有的钱都偷走了，还对你拳打脚踢。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: To some extent, it is.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上说，确实如此。

sentences.en: And the beating up, Tom.
sentences.zh: 还有殴打，托姆。

sentences.en: So let's get into this.
sentences.zh: 我们这就开始讲。

sentences.en: Overnight, when the Nazis moved in, they took control of the Austrian police records.
sentences.zh: 一夜之间，当纳粹入驻时，他们接管了奥地利警察局的档案。

sentences.en: And they detained, in one evening, 21,000 people.
sentences.zh: 就在一个晚上，他们拘捕了两万一千人。

sentences.en: This is a scale of repression that astounds and horrifies Europe.
sentences.zh: 这种规模的镇压让欧洲震惊且惊恐。

sentences.en: Some people are killed.
sentences.zh: 有些人被杀害了。

sentences.en: Lots of people, sort of Nazi critics, flee.
sentences.zh: 许多人，也就是纳粹的批评者们，逃跑了。

sentences.en: Schuschnigg didn't flee.
sentences.zh: 许士尼格没有逃跑。

sentences.en: And actually, he ended up in prison, didn't he, Tom?
sentences.zh: 事实上，他最后进了监狱，对吧，托姆？

sentences.en: He ends up in a concentration camp, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想他最后进了一个集中营。

sentences.en: Yeah, he ends up in a concentration camp.
sentences.zh: 是的，他最后进了集中营。

sentences.en: And he almost dies at the end of the war.
sentences.zh: 而且他在战争快结束时差点死掉。

sentences.en: But along with other kind of very distinguished prisoners, he escapes.
sentences.zh: 但和其他一些非常杰出的囚犯一起，他逃了出来。

sentences.en: He ends up as a professor in St. Louis.
sentences.zh: 他最终成了圣路易斯的一名教授。

sentences.en: He becomes a US citizen.
sentences.zh: 他成了美国公民。

sentences.en: Yeah, he does.
sentences.zh: 是的，他确实成了。

sentences.en: Extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 太非同寻常了。

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 他的确如此。

sentences.en: I noticed that, too.
sentences.zh: 我也注意到了这一点。

sentences.en: I thought, what a strange, very Kerensky kind of behavior.
sentences.zh: 我想，这行为可真奇怪，太像克伦斯基了。

sentences.en: I wonder if they had academic conferences in America in the 19th.
sentences.zh: 我在想，19世纪他们在美国有没有开过学术会议。

sentences.en: It's for all the people who had previously run countries that had been taken over by dictators.
sentences.zh: 那是为所有以前管理过被独裁者接管的国家的那些人准备的。

sentences.en: Anyway, various other people are killed.
sentences.zh: 总之，还有其他各种各样的人被杀。

sentences.en: And what about the Jews?
sentences.zh: 那犹太人呢？

sentences.en: The worst of the repression obviously falls on Austria's Jews.
sentences.zh: 最严重的镇压显然落在了奥地利犹太人头上。

sentences.en: And this is really where we start to get into the kind of the real darkness.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们开始切入真正的黑暗之处。

sentences.en: So there are about 200,000 Jews in Austria.
sentences.zh: 奥地利大约有二十万犹太人。

sentences.en: And the vast, vast majority of them lived in Vienna.
sentences.zh: 其中绝大多数都住在维也纳。

sentences.en: Now, we talked right at the very beginning of our first Nazi series about the intense anti-Semitism that Hitler had encountered as a young man in Vienna before the First World War.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们在第一季纳粹系列的最初就谈过希特勒在第一次世界大战前作为年轻人维也纳见闻的强烈反犹太主义。

sentences.en: That it had a virulence and a venom that was well beyond anything in Germany at the same time.
sentences.zh: 它带有那种远超德国同时期任何事物的恶毒与刻薄。

sentences.en: And the reaction to the Anschluss in Vienna is absolutely horrifying.
sentences.zh: 而维也纳对德奥合并的反应绝对令人毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: So almost all Jewish-owned businesses in Vienna are taken over straight away.
sentences.zh: 因此，维也纳几乎所有犹太人拥有的企业都被直接接管了。

sentences.en: Jewish business leaders are killed.
sentences.zh: 犹太商界领袖被杀害。

sentences.en: Companies like Deutsche Bank or IG Farben blithely, you know, once they're dead, they take over their enterprises.
sentences.zh: 像德意志银行或法本公司这样的大企业，高高兴兴地，你知道的，一旦他们死了，就接管了他们的企业。

sentences.en: And don't they get the Jewish heads of banks into cars and kind of chuck them out when they're going at 80 miles an hour?
sentences.zh: 他们不是还把犹太银行行长们塞进汽车里，然后在车开到每小时80英里的时候把他们扔出去吗？

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: The guy who runs the Credit Anstalt, which is probably the biggest bank in Central Europe, he was thrown out of a car.
sentences.zh: 经营信贷银行的那个家伙，可能是中欧最大的银行，他就是被从车里扔出来的。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: And the notorious scenes are that Jews are made to scrub anti-Nazi slogans from the streets.
sentences.zh: 那些臭名昭著的场景是，犹太人被迫从街上擦洗反纳粹标语。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: While people watch and kind of throw cold water over them and flick acid at them.
sentences.zh: 同时人们在一旁围观，往他们身上泼冷水，还向他们泼酸液。

sentences.en: Horrible scenes.
sentences.zh: 可怕的场景。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Vienna was a very political city, so it was covered with political graffiti.
sentences.zh: 维也纳是一个政治氛围很浓的城市，所以到处都是政治涂鸦。

sentences.en: A lot of it, you know, Schussnig's partisans, he had controlled the biggest party in Austria.
sentences.zh: 其中很多，你知道的，是许士尼格的支持者留下的，他曾控制着奥地利最大的政党。

sentences.en: So there's loads of pro-Schussnig graffiti.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多支持许士尼格的涂鸦。

sentences.en: Groups of Jews, men and women, young and old, kids, the elderly, whatever, they're dragged out by so-called cleaning squads and they are forced to scrub these slogans.
sentences.zh: 一群群的犹太人，男女老少，从孩子到老人，不管是谁，都被所谓的清洁小分队拖出来，强迫他们擦洗这些标语。

sentences.en: And groups of people, you can see photos, you can read the newspaper reports, they're horrific.
sentences.zh: 人群，你可以看到照片，你可以读到报纸报道，他们太可怕了。

sentences.en: Groups of people would stand around them, jeering at them, kicking them, punching them, spitting at them, throwing cold water over them, as you say.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，人群围着他们，嘲笑他们，踢他们，殴打他们，吐口水，往他们身上泼冷水。

sentences.en: There was a guy called George Gedier, who was the correspondent for the Daily Telegraph, and he wrote these really,
sentences.zh: 有个叫乔治·吉迪尔的家伙，他是《每日电讯报》的记者，他写了这些极其……

sentences.en: really harrowing kind of dispatches from Vienna about the mobs of Nazis standing around these people.
sentences.zh: 非常令人揪心的来自维也纳的电讯，关于纳粹暴徒围着这些人的报道。

sentences.en: As you said, throwing acid at them and laughing at them.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，向他们泼酸液并嘲笑他们。

sentences.en: And these Nazis are Austrian.
sentences.zh: 而这些纳粹都是奥地利人。

sentences.en: Austrian Nazis.
sentences.zh: 奥地利纳粹。

sentences.en: Austrian Nazis and frankly, Tom, ordinary Austrians.
sentences.zh: 奥地利纳粹，坦白说，托姆，还有普通的奥地利人。

sentences.en: Well, because there's a story, isn't there, of a guy looking out of a window and seeing a policeman beating up a Jew.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为有个故事，对吧，有个家伙看着窗外，看到一个警察在痛打一个犹太人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And he realises that this is a policeman he's known all his life.
sentences.zh: 然后他意识到这是他认识了一辈子的警察。

sentences.en: Exactly, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，对。

sentences.en: Didn't they have it in him?
sentences.zh: 他们怎么能下得去手？

sentences.en: A guy called, he ended up being called George Clare because he moved to England.
sentences.zh: 有个叫……他后来因为搬去了英国，叫乔治·克莱尔。

sentences.en: He was called Georg Klar.
sentences.zh: 他原本叫格奥尔格·克拉尔。

sentences.en: And he wrote a book called Last Waltz in Vienna, which I really recommend to the listeners if they want to read more about this.
sentences.zh: 他写了一本书叫《维也纳的最后华尔兹》，如果听众想了解更多这方面的信息，我真的向大家推荐。

sentences.en: You can completely understand why you wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 你完全可以理解为什么你不会去看。

sentences.en: And he describes, as you say, looking out of his window, seeing the faces contorted with hatred and the people he knows.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他描述了自己望向窗外，看到那些因仇恨而扭曲的面孔，以及他认识的人。

sentences.en: Neighbours and things.
sentences.zh: 邻居之类的人。

sentences.en: A lot of Jews try to flee to the Czech border.
sentences.zh: 许多犹太人试图逃往捷克边境。

sentences.en: It's terrible.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了。

sentences.en: Thousands, they get onto the last trains and stuff, but people ambush them at the stations and they're taking their property, beating them up.
sentences.zh: 成千上万的人挤上最后的列车之类，但在车站有人伏击他们，抢夺他们的财产，殴打他们。

sentences.en: When they get to the Czech border, the Czechs are turning them back.
sentences.zh: 当他们到达捷克边境时，捷克人把他们赶了回去。

sentences.en: So they're trying to get through the woods and stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以他们试图穿过树林之类的地方。

sentences.en: They're in kind of no man's land.
sentences.zh: 他们处于某种三不管地带。

sentences.en: Loads of people kill themselves.
sentences.zh: 很多人自杀。

sentences.en: Hundreds of people.
sentences.zh: 成百上千的人。

sentences.en: Suicide rate massively goes up because it's obvious to a lot of people at this point, a lot of Jewish people.
sentences.zh: 自杀率大幅上升，因为此时对很多人来说，很多犹太人来说，一切已经显而易见。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, most famously, Sigmund Freud has already left.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，最著名的西格蒙德·弗洛伊德已经离开了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That, you know, we are plunged into this unbelievable nightmare.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们陷入了这个难以置信的噩梦。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, Tom, just to wrap up, because I know we've been talking at great length.
sentences.zh: 所以，托姆，简单总结一下，因为我知道我们已经聊了很久了。

sentences.en: But there's one terrible omen of the future, which is that in the face of all this, the Nazis think, you know, let's kick all these Jews out.
sentences.zh: 但未来有一个可怕的预兆，那就是面对这一切，纳粹心想，你知道的，把这些犹太人都赶走吧。

sentences.en: Because they've now got an extra 200,000 Jews, which is about the number that's already emigrated from Germany.
sentences.zh: 因为他们现在多了二十万犹太人，这大约是已经从德国移民出去的人数。

sentences.en: Yes, roughly.
sentences.zh: 是的，差不多。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So they're basically now back to square one as far as they see it.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上在他们看来，现在又回到了原点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And they set up a central agency for Jewish emigration that is going to work in collaboration with some handpicked Jewish leaders.
sentences.zh: 他们建立了一个犹太人移民中央机构，将与一些精挑细选的犹太人领袖合作。

sentences.en: And the guy they get to run that is a man from the SS.
sentences.zh: 他们找来负责这个的人是一个党卫军成员。

sentences.en: And he is a man called Adolf Eichmann, who had lived in Austria before the First World War.
sentences.zh: 他叫阿道夫·艾希曼，第一次世界大战前曾在奥地利生活过。

sentences.en: Eichmann is fanatical, but he's also incredibly methodical.
sentences.zh: 艾希曼是个狂热分子，但他也极其有条理。

sentences.en: And he works, you know, he's a bureaucrat.
sentences.zh: 他工作，你知道的，他就是个官僚。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And in his compiling of lists and all of this, you can see a pattern that will recur in an even more sinister form during the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 在整理名单和所有这些事情的过程中，你可以看到一种模式，它将在第二次世界大战中以更加阴险的形式重演。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: One other quick point before we pack up.
sentences.zh: 在我们结束之前还有个小问题。

sentences.en: This obviously has a colossal impact on Hitler himself.
sentences.zh: 这显然对希特勒本人产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: He returns more popular than ever in Germany, greeted with an enormous, overwhelming explosion of joy.
sentences.zh: 他回到德国时比以往任何时候都更受欢迎，迎接他的是巨大、排山倒海般的喜悦爆发。

sentences.en: He has fulfilled almost all of the ambitions now of German nationalists.
sentences.zh: 他现在几乎实现了德国民族主义者的所有野心。

sentences.en: So all of the stuff he's done so far is what any militaristic, authoritarian, conservative, sort of irredentist German leader would have done.
sentences.zh: 所以他到目前为止所做的一切，都是任何军国主义、威权主义、保守主义的领土收复主义德国领导人会做的事。

sentences.en: And he's done it without provoking war, without provoking war.
sentences.zh: 而且他做到这一切时没有挑起战争，没有挑起战争。

sentences.en: An astounding achievement.
sentences.zh: 了不起的成就。

sentences.en: And yet, yeah, the whole thing about Hitler is that it is not enough.
sentences.zh: 然而，是的，关于希特勒的全部问题就在于这还远远不够。

sentences.en: He has got more stuff lined up.
sentences.zh: 他已经安排好了更多的事情。

sentences.en: And even as this is ending within days, he says to Goebbels, right, Czechoslovakia next.
sentences.zh: 甚至当这一切刚结束几天后，他就对戈培尔说，好，下一个是捷克斯洛伐克。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: You talked about how Jews are strong-armed into emigration or are trying to escape across the border and committing suicide there or being shot or whatever.
sentences.zh: 你谈到犹太人是如何被强行逼迫移民，或者试图逃过边境并在那里自杀、被枪杀等等。

sentences.en: Just to go back to another famous group of exiles from Germany, the von Trapps, who we began with.
sentences.zh: 回想起另一个著名的德国流亡群体，也就是我们开篇提到的冯·特拉普一家。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Anyone who has seen the film will remember that they go by foot over the Alps into Switzerland.
sentences.zh: 任何看过这部电影的人都会记得他们是步行翻越阿尔卑斯山进入瑞士的。

sentences.en: That is not actually what happened.
sentences.zh: 事实并非如此。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: Because Georg von Trapp, you know, he was an army officer.
sentences.zh: 因为格奥尔格·冯·特拉普，你知道的，他是一名军官。

sentences.en: He wasn't Jewish.
sentences.zh: 他不是犹太人。

sentences.en: There were no restrictions on his travel whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 他的旅行没有任何限制。

sentences.en: So even though the German high command were very keen that he go to Bremenhaven and join the Krieg Marine there, he doesn't.
sentences.zh: 所以尽管德国最高统帅部非常希望他去不莱梅港加入那里的海军，但他没有去。

sentences.en: He takes his family.
sentences.zh: 他带着他的家人。

sentences.en: They get on a train and they go to Italy.
sentences.zh: 他们上了火车去了意大利。

sentences.en: And from there they go to London and from there to the United States.
sentences.zh: 从那里他们去了伦敦，然后从那里去美国。

sentences.en: So it's easy for some people to get out of Austria and less easy for others.
sentences.zh: 所以有些人离开奥地利很容易，而另一些人则没那么容易。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Because as you say, had he been Jewish.
sentences.zh: 因为正如你所说，如果他是犹太人。

sentences.en: It would have been a very different story.
sentences.zh: 那将会是完全不同的故事了。

sentences.en: It would have been a totally different story.
sentences.zh: 那将是一个完全不同的故事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So in the next episode, we're going to try and see the world through Nazi eyes.
sentences.zh: 所以在下一集中，我们将尝试通过纳粹的视角来看世界。

sentences.en: We're going to try and understand how the Nazis themselves viewed what they were doing as being the right thing to do.
sentences.zh: 我们将试着理解纳粹自己是如何看待他们所做的事情是正确之举的。

sentences.en: They weren't sitting around saying, are we the baddies?
sentences.zh: 他们不会坐在一起问，我们是坏蛋吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.zh: 并审视移民和迫害的过程，多米尼克，

sentences.zh: 所以这是一个略显阴暗的结局，托姆。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.zh: 本周的节目。

sentences.zh: 但这是一个沉重的主题。

sentences.zh: 但也是非常重要的主题。
